messages.subject: (more) publicity for the spOccupancy package
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

at the Swiss Ornithological Institute, we’re interested in producing routine species distribution maps for a large number of bird species year-round, e.g. every month, based on checklist data containing detection/nondetections. If possible, our preference would be to use some SDM that explicitly takes into account imperfect detection, i.e., some sort of occupancy model. Over the last days I have been experimenting with different model fitting functions in the spOccupancy package (https://www.jeffdoser.com/files/spoccupancy-web/) and found them to be really good.

Different types of spatial and spatio-temporal occupancy models can be fit in very reasonable time (i.e., minutes rather than hours or days as with BUGS software) to data sets with many 1000’s of sites and then I make predictions to the 42,000 km2 of the country again in just a couple of minutes. One of the latest additions to the package is spatially-varying coefficient (SVC) models, which can be fit both as a “simple” binomial GLM and as an occupancy model.

If you like occupancy models and colorful species distribution maps, then you should really check this package out. ESPECIALLY, if you have large data sets.

(And no, I don’t have any direct financial interests in the package 😊..)

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.subject: Quantitative Postdoc - Alaska
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

We're looking for a quantitatively-minded postdoc to work on issues related to partial detection, multiple data sources, and variable detection rates in spatial-capture-recapture and spatial-mark-resight models in Alaska, with a major focus on wolves.  Please see the detailed description (attached) and feel free to send this along to anyone who may be interested.  Thanks!

Shawn

ensemble methods applied to marine ecosystems, based in Maths & Stats in
Sheffield and supervised by me and by Mike Spence and Chris Lynam at the
Centre for Environment, Fisheries and Aquaculture Science. The project

May 2023.

becoming available.

Paul.
